concepts.definition: Semantic Import applies the FOUNDATIONS import definition to a declared target scope, preserving unchanged meaning, direction, loss and lack of authority. Semantic Translation declares directional meaning change and loss and is not an import. Semantic Equivalence requires governing authorities to establish equality while each concept retains its owner and context; neither spelling nor opposing translations proves it. Semantic Disambiguation selects one meaning for one scope without equating competitors; a selected foreign concept enters only through a declared import, translation or equivalence.

grounding.quote: | Semantic Disambiguation | not an import: it selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. Where the selected concept is owned in another bounded context, it enters that scope only by the import, translation or equivalence its carrier declares (§6) |

| Semantic Equivalence | not an import: each concept keeps its own owner and context, and neither adopts the other's meaning. It requires the governing authorities to establish the claimed equality; neither identical spelling nor two opposing translations proves it automatically |

Historical installs and unrelated content remain available and unchanged; create no consumer-local checker and change neither Product meaning nor local semantic map.

grounding.quote:
For each selected derived context, missing, ambiguous, changed or
unavailable program, map or source evidence holds the complete update
before any consumer effect.

constraints.statement: Missing, ambiguous, changed or unavailable program/map/source evidence holds the whole update before consumer effects. The source owner performs needed semantic re-entry; the manager cannot mechanically relabel an old map current. Exact freshness establishes integrity, not semantic conformance or an independent verdict. After immutable staging, recheck consumer preimages and source evidence; report completion only after verifying every selected resulting binding and companion.

exceptions: Newly staged immutable installs may remain unused.

grounding.quote:
The operation requires an exclusive consumer
write scope during application. It claims no crash-atomic transaction
across independent filesystem paths

constraints.statement: Refusal before consumer effects retains prior state. Caught application failure restores affected preimages and does not report completion. Application requires an exclusive consumer write scope. There is no crash-atomic claim across independent paths: abrupt process/host loss or unavailable rollback storage requires recovery from presented preimages before claiming the complete relation.

conditions: The operation has an intended external effect, as install, sync, mutating adopt, fleet adoption or complete update does.

grounding.quote:
- Effect. An operation that writes, such as `install`, `sync`, a mutating
  `adopt`, fleet adoption or the complete consumer update, has an
  intended external effect, recorded under
  [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) for the predicate "the
  intended effect occurred". Reported completion is `completed`
  (`satisfied`) only where evidence about the subject establishes the
  effect in full, as the complete update's verification of every
  selected resulting binding and companion does. The cause selects the
  other values. A refusal before any effect, with the retained prior
  state as the evidence about the subject, is `not_effected`
  (`falsified`), and the effect has ended. A caught application failure
  is also `not_effected` (`falsified`): the failure observed on the
  subject establishes that the complete update is not attained, and the
  operation applies no later part of it, so no later completion of this
  effect can attain it. Whether its restored preimages are verified
  decides only whether the effect's end is established, never the value:
  verified, the effect has ended; a restoration not verified, or rollback
  storage unavailable after the failure, leaves the end not established,
  recorded beside the value as a residual naming the verification that
  would establish it. Newly staged immutable installs left unused are
  named with the value as the part that did occur. Abrupt process or
  host loss, where no caught failure establishes that the update fell
  short, is `completion_unknown` (`indeterminate`), never `completed` or
  `not_effected`. `completion_unknown`, and `not_effected` with its end
  not established, are effects of uncertain completion under
  [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects): recovery from the
  presented preimages reconciles them, as
  [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart) states, before
  any repetition or claim of the complete relation.

constraints.statement: For 'the intended effect occurred', completed maps to satisfied only when subject evidence establishes the whole effect. Pre-effect refusal maps to not_effected/falsified with ended effect and retained prior state as evidence. Caught application failure also maps to not_effected/falsified because the full update fell short and no later part is applied; restoration verification decides only whether its end is established. Verified restoration establishes the end; unverified restoration or unavailable rollback storage leaves the end unestablished, with a residual naming needed verification. Record unused staged installs as the part that occurred. Abrupt process/host loss without a caught failure establishing shortfall maps to completion_unknown/indeterminate, never completed or not_effected. completion_unknown and not_effected with unestablished end require reconciliation from presented preimages before repetition or a complete-relation claim.

conditions: An operation refuses application on its exact bound subject and basis.

grounding.quote:
- Refusal. A refusal also answers whether the operation may apply its
  effect on the exact subject and basis it binds. Found before the
  operation begins, it is an outcome of
  [ACTIVATION §3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation),
  for "the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject
  and basis"; found after it has begun, as by the recheck after immutable
  staging, it is a value of
  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability),
  for "a candidate is available". A missing explicit acceptance of the
  exact plan, or missing whole-selection authorisation of a fleet write,
  is missing operation authority: `admission_refused(authority)`
  (`out_of_frame`), naming the acceptance or authorisation needed and
  its owner. Every other refusal has a basis cause: drift of the Product
  Definition bytes or of a consumer preimage; a stale plan; each other
  condition of the fail-closed list above, ambiguous discovery included
  because it leaves no exact subject; a path, locator or marker span that
  escapes or breaks its boundary; and missing, ambiguous, changed or
  unavailable derived-context evidence, which holds the complete update.
  It is `admission_refused(basis)` before the operation begins and
  `re_entry_requested(basis)` after, `invalid_basis` in both, and names
  the basis coordinate that fails and, for derived-context evidence, the
  source owner whose re-entry repairs it.

constraints.statement: Before commencement, refusal answers lawful admission/activation; after commencement, including post-staging recheck, it answers construction availability. Missing exact-plan acceptance or whole-selection fleet-write authorisation is admission_refused(authority)/out_of_frame and names the needed authority and owner. Every other refusal has a basis cause: definition/preimage drift, stale plan, referenced fail-closed conditions including ambiguous discovery with no exact subject, escaping/broken path/locator/marker boundary, or defective derived evidence. Basis refusal is admission_refused(basis) before commencement and re_entry_requested(basis) after, both invalid_basis; name the failing coordinate and, for derived evidence, the repairing source owner.
constraints.uncertainty: The full fail-closed list is referenced but not supplied.

grounding.quote:
- Command without an intended effect. A command without an intended
  external effect, such as `verify` or `adopt --dry-run`, has no value
  under Effects, and its refusal maps by cause as above. A condition it
  reports about the subject it evaluates, such as a member that `verify`
  finds missing, extra or changed, is a counterexample to that command's
  own predicate, `falsified`, not a refusal.

Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines the manager's
outcomes with other results cannot read a refused or failed operation as
completed, an operation whose value is `completion_unknown` as either
completed or not effected, a caught failure whose restoration is not
verified as undecided when the update is known to have fallen short, or
a refusal for missing acceptance as one for a defective basis (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Effectless verify and adopt --dry-run have no Effects value, though refusals still map by cause. Missing/extra/changed members observed by verify falsify its own predicate and are not refusals. Composition with other results must not turn refusal/failure into completion, completion_unknown into completed or not_effected, known caught failure with unverified restoration into undecided value, or missing acceptance into defective basis.

grounding.quote:
A bounded context exists only when an owning authority declares its stable
identity, owner, selected basis and governed semantic scope.

constraints.statement: Context existence requires an owning authority's declaration of stable identity, owner, basis and scope. A consuming member defines a concept in it only through an explicit owner relation. Filename, heading, index/glossary row, schema value or bare URI cannot constitute it. Equal spelling/capitalisation/shape/location/nesting/actor/implementation establishes neither equal meaning, identity, equivalence, inheritance nor authority; different spelling does not prove different meaning. Such relations require the semantic address or explicit authorised relation.

conditions: A material occurrence is being resolved.

grounding.quote:
4. apply every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; and
5. admit the occurrence only when exactly one concept remains.

constraints.statement: Resolve in order: identify governed scope and nearest explicit context declaration; identify exact basis and applicable authorities; collect admitted local definitions and explicit imports; apply every applicable owner-authorised override/disambiguation; admit only if exactly one concept remains. An owning document/section/schema field/operation may declare context for subordinate occurrences, avoiding repeated qualifiers in uniquely resolved prose. Repositories, directories, filenames, headings, glossary matches, prompts, actors or nearby definitions do not declare context accidentally.

conditions: Zero or multiple applicable concepts remain at a material boundary.

grounding.quote:
Zero applicable concepts is unresolved meaning; more than one is ambiguous
meaning. Both fail closed at a material boundary:

constraints.statement: Zero concepts is unresolved; multiple concepts is ambiguous. Agents, designs, schemas, implementations, tests, translations and reviewers must not choose by familiarity, frequency, recency, nominal match or context-free glossary fallback. A dependent evaluation returns out_of_frame and names the missing definition/import/disambiguation relation and owner, or indeterminate when admissible evidence also cannot decide the claim, naming that ground too. In either case the ground is explicit; unresolved meaning is not false meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: The external core rule deciding these result grounds is referenced, not fully supplied.

grounding.quote: - the preserved meaning, changed meaning, loss and refusal conditions;

constraints.statement: Every carrier states exact source/target concept references and context identities; kind (unchanged import, disambiguation, directional translation including specialisation, or stronger equivalence); direction and lawful inverse where material; preserved/changed meaning, loss and refusal conditions; both semantic owners without authority transfer; both selected bases, scope and provenance; lifecycle and invalidation. Semantic owners are authorities, distinct from owning clauses. The member-import rule applies between any two authority-declared contexts; changed, narrowed or lost source meaning is not an import. None of the four kinds widens source or target authority, and translation/equivalence/disambiguation cannot pass as unchanged import.

grounding.quote:
- `resolves_to`: the exact selected concept reference, which is one member
  of `disambiguates`;

constraints.statement: Every local entry names its decision URI, existing lawful Product/requirement/accepted-design/other authority, overridden clause or resolved ambiguity where applicable, and exact scope. Each local_constitution.disambiguations binding additionally names exact term, context identity, complete material candidate concept/clause references, resolves_to as one candidate, every needed semantic basis, and uri/authority/applies_to. The URI owns resolution; crossing contexts requires its complete §5 import/translation/equivalence relation. Empty arrays explicitly declare no bound entries of that kind; omission is not equivalent.

grounding.quote:
The JSON entry locates that
declaration and its authority relation; it does not contain the binding,
adopt the profile, restate the frames or create frame-set authority (P6).

constraints.statement: reference_frame_bases is non-empty; each entry names an accepted declaration URI, every existing admitting authority and exact governed Product/context/tenant/outcome/other scope. The declaration owns frame set, method/profile basis, outcome, actor rules, envelopes, grants, triggers, coverage, results and invalidation. REFERENCE_FRAME supplies principles and declaration shape, and the Executive baseline supplies only an optional profile; neither selects, adopts or owns a Product binding. Existing Product authority owns the declaration and every grant. Profile availability through method-cut inclusion, Product adoption and exact-work-instruction activation are distinct relations.

grounding.quote:
An Agent Frame Activation does not mutate the overlay, and the overlay
registers no agents, assigns no permanent frames and persists no temporary
active frame configuration

constraints.statement: Activation does not mutate the overlay, which registers no agents, assigns no permanent frames and persists no temporary configuration. Frames and actors retain distinct identities; actor name or broad frame grants no semantic/operation/review/acceptance/disposition authority beyond cited owners and exact activation. For outcomes crossing a Product chain, the collective basis records a Product-role map distinguishing mutable projects, definitions, candidate checkpoints, release cuts, released Products, installs, artifacts and dependents; development products are role bindings over exact install identities. Every directed composition edge names roles, governing authority/contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and invalidation. Shared actors/repositories/files/implementations/outputs/tools establish no identity or composition. A same-named runtime/domain Frame enters a collective frame set only by explicit declaration with evaluation and authority relations; otherwise it remains under bound WHAT/HOW and may be an evaluation subject or coordinate.

grounding.quote:
A separate
`TENANT_REGISTRY.md` may remain as a human-readable companion or generated
projection and cannot become a second tenant-identity or location
authority

constraints.statement: Intent and Product each have one canonical entrypoint; specification may cite several surfaces. Each tenant has stable identity and root/design/implementation locators, with the binding governed by SPEC_METHOD §11. A separate TENANT_REGISTRY.md may be a companion or projection, never a second tenant-identity/location authority. Work bindings locate carriers without deciding which carrier an item takes; SPEC_METHOD §4 and TICKETS own that choice. Ticket lanes include at least backlog, active and completed.

grounding.quote:
For a requested Product scope exactly one applicable definition is
selected; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and a
symlinked definition is refused

constraints.statement: Select exactly one applicable definition for a requested Product scope; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed and symlinked definitions are refused. Nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition or override. Each explicit edge names product_definition locator, target_definition_id matching target product.definition_id, directed relation authority defining roles/owner/scope/lifecycle/invalidation, and one or more exact governing contracts. Resolve locator and identity: moving requires a locator update but preserves identity; replacement with another identity at the same locator fails closed. If the edge binds immutable Product/release versions, relation and contracts must also carry and verify those identities; mutable definition identity cannot substitute.

grounding.quote: A conforming discovered set satisfies all of the following (P3, P6, P1):

constraints.statement: Every definition validates against its selected released schema; every required URI/fragment resolves within declared workspace/resolver boundaries; definition IDs are globally unique in the set and tenant IDs unique within each overlay; every governed scope has a resolvable applicable frame basis with overlaps reconciled by cited authority; every disambiguation has exact term/context, complete candidates, selected candidate member, authority/basis/scope and congruent carrier; every material cross-context seam has explicit semantic relation; every composition target identity, relation and non-empty contract set resolves; no two carriers claim authority over the same Product, tenant, ticket state or constitutional relation.

grounding.quote:
The structural subset and
the semantic subset of these checks are distinct claims

constraints.statement: Portable Draft 2020-12 validation establishes shape. uri and uri-reference are annotations unless the validator asserts formats. Conformance therefore explicitly checks RFC 3986 URI/reference syntax with an assertion-capable validator, then separately checks resolution, fragments, selected-release identity, cross-file uniqueness, constitutional sufficiency, semantic resolution, cross-context-relation completeness and authority congruence. Structural and semantic subsets are separate claims.

grounding.quote:
Correct
downstream behaviour produced through a guessed meaning does not pass
semantic conformance

constraints.statement: Without an explicit cross-context relation, Frame/Owner/Product/Tenant candidates remain distinct: no runtime-frame enrolment, specialist owner authority or default tenancy inference; Product is selected only through declared occurrence context. User is unresolved pending downstream definition/relation. Positive local cases declare one context and exactly one concept; positive cross-context cases supply a complete authorised relation. Negative cases cover zero candidates, multiple after disambiguation, selection outside candidates, context-free glossary fallback, incomplete coordinates, authority/basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidated relations. Correct output reached through guessed meaning fails semantic conformance. CONFORMANCE may index but not redefine these cases.

grounding.quote:
A projected prohibition cannot lose its condition
or its lawful alternative, even when every source digest is correct.

constraints.statement: Compressions, templates, comments, candidates, installs and mutable source are derived/evidential/authoring surfaces, not selectable partial constitutions or reinterpretations of owners. Derived instructions preserve applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision owners and invalidators within scope; compression cannot strengthen/weaken a relation or drop a prohibition's condition/lawful alternative. References must resolve within actor access or supply needed meaning directly. Cut/install derived surfaces carry paths and digests of every deciding source and watched index; any digest change makes them stale, requiring regeneration or explicit re-acceptance before current treatment. Raw owners in the same selected cut decide questions a stale/insufficient carrier cannot decide.
constraints.uncertainty: The full external staleness, standalone-scope and digest-evidence laws are not supplied.

exceptions: Concrete form is method law when explicitly accepted by the method as an interoperability boundary, as the referenced definition schema/template are.

grounding.quote:
A shared-method amendment cannot create an executable tool, workflow
engine, runtime, assurance system or consumer realisation as STDO Product
scope without separate explicit human authorisation.

constraints.statement: Consumers own instantiated types/schemas/files/tools/runtime/orchestration/tests/executable conformance; method ownership of abstract law does not generally prescribe these forms. Creating executable tooling, workflow engines, runtime, assurance systems or consumer realisations as STDO Product scope by shared-method amendment requires separate explicit human authorisation. Recording a ruling cannot widen subject, implication, authority or change class. Only a released method version is publication authority; mutable source may author a future cut but must not silently govern consumers.

exceptions: A project-local exact copy is lawful when explicitly bound and verified, though not the default.

grounding.quote:
A project creates no competing local methodology root, such as a default
`specification/standards/`, and binds no mutable or partial method source
as if it were the selected immutable release

constraints.statement: Mutable method authoring belongs in its source workspace and governs a future candidate only. Released authority is the consumer-selected exact immutable version; installed distribution normally uses the shared store and matches basis URI/manifest digest. Project constitutional authority lives at WHAT bindings, realisation/work at HOW/ticketing. No competing local method root or mutable/partial source may impersonate the selected release. During editing/repricing, mutable source is candidate-authoring authority, not consumer law before release and explicit selection. The resolved installed basis remains operative distribution until explicit adoption of another cut; proximity cannot select a local copy.

grounding.quote: The bootstrap sequence is (P3, P6, P2):

constraints.statement: The described sequence is: (1) install manager once, resolve one version-line selector and explicitly select an immutable RC; (2) install complete cut in shared store and retain deterministic manifest digest; (3) copy exact-cut template to named/default definition; (4) assign stable mutable definition-line ID, source-project locator and context, distinct from immutable Product/releases; (5) bind constitutional source, non-operative selector, exact basis/digest, additional authorities and basis-qualified entrypoints, confirming collective axioms/ontology/epistemology/taxonomy/semantics; (6) bind bootstrap/portable targets relative to resolved source_project, preflight all and refresh only marker-bounded discovery blocks; (7) bind or explicitly empty each local collection; (8) bind at least one accepted collective frame basis with authorities/scope; (9) confirm Goals, run Goals→Intent→Product and bind entrypoints; (10) gather/derive/classify/bind live requirements without co-equal rival; (11) bind at least one tenant with root/design/implementation and shared law; (12) bind Goals, ticket lanes, comments and optional sprint root; (13) bind every known composition edge with target ID, relation authority and non-empty contracts; (14) validate shape, assert URI syntax, synchronise/verify exact installed basis, resolve every URI and check cross-definition identity, composition, constitutional sufficiency and authority congruence.
constraints.uncertainty: This records the source's sequence without performing it.

conditions: A bound requirement set has become the live constitutional surface.

grounding.quote:
Once a bound requirement set is the live constitutional surface, no rival
monolithic requirements document should remain co-equal authority with it.

constraints.statement: No rival monolithic requirements document should remain co-equal authority with the live set. This is the source's recommendation, intended to keep requirement truth clear, derivable and non-monolithic without prescribing its folder.

exceptions: Externally owned terms may appear in core disposition tables.
The tier-1 traversal record, F_D/F_P/F_H and generic 'module' are not restricted by this exclusion.

grounding.quote: The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor.

constraints.statement: Externally owned profile/realisation/rc.2 terms do not enter tiers 1–2: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, IACS and Prime are named examples. A profile may bind core mechanisms to such terms only by a declared direction, preserved meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. Worked applications, hello worlds and data mappers remain external test subjects; particulars do not become generic functionality by precedent.

grounding.quote:
A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds

constraints.statement: A profile imports each used tier-1/2 concept and generic family under FOUNDATIONS §2, restating none of their rules, and owns only its added domain/operation terms and choices. Its family table follows FOUNDATIONS §3 and names imported family IDs and table sections in the premise column; rules rest on those consequences with their original standing and owners. Refinement of another profile is declared in the lead; the refined profile retains its rules. Generic rules gain no second owner and added choices are not presented as foundational consequences.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced import and consequence-standing rules are not fully supplied.

conditions: A received predecessor row lacks a disposition.

grounding.quote:
a
row with none is unresolved, which blocks qualification of the claim it
affects.

constraints.statement: Each predecessor disposition must take one of RELEASE §9's four values. No disposition means unresolved and blocks qualification of the affected claim; it is not an inferred conservation or supersession.
constraints.uncertainty: The four-value domain itself is referenced but not enumerated in the supplied section.

grounding.quote: It is an optional derived surface under ACTIVATION §2 Acquisition; for a task it does not cover, acquire the deciding owner sections.

constraints.statement: The indexed acquisition rule uses a derived surface with current sources when it serves the task, otherwise deciding owner sections. Verbatim frames and constraint surfaces projected from a current a_c interpretation are examples. The i3 interpretation is optional; its README determines coverage and insufficiency, and uncovered tasks require owner sections. Earlier a_c sets are historical, not current. These are described routes, not performed acquisition.

grounding.quote:
The corpus is applicable
without the rc.2 cut, which remains the operative builder of this
construction until this candidate is released.

constraints.statement: Constitutional membership comprises tiers 1–2 and project-selected tier-3 profiles. Each clause names its requiring principle. Predecessor routes are provenance, not dispositions; dispositions use RELEASE §9 values, are recorded in each receiving member's final section, and are indexed with loci in the tenant frontier. The source claims candidate applicability without the predecessor cut while retaining rc.2 as operative builder until release. Verbatim frames remain non-deciding copies and their use versus owner sections follows external ACTIVATION acquisition law.
constraints.uncertainty: Applicability is a source claim, not an acceptance or release judgment here.

exceptions: An explicitly bound and verified project-local copy remains possible, but is not the default.

grounding.quote:
Installed bytes take their authority from the exact RC cut, the product
definition's basis URI, the manifest digest and the member inventory

constraints.statement: The manager installs each complete immutable cut once in a shared versioned store and resolves logical release URIs. Product definitions name basis by logical URI and manifest digest, without machine-local paths. Installed authority derives from exact RC cut, basis URI, manifest digest and member inventory. Mutable authoring head and moving version-line selector never silently replace the selected consumer basis.

grounding.quote:
"Atomic" is said at engagement altitude only. It does not assert that every
relation inside the frame is one irreducible semantic atom;

constraints.statement: Frame-set selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are separate functions. Engagement atomicity does not imply semantic irreducibility: multiple atoms and owners can coexist without merged meaning/authority; no universal theory of all relationships is prerequisite. Engagement law defines no application profile, role mapping, Product frame-basis binding, domain Product, specification taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption relation or assurance implementation. External imports/specialisations under other owners do not enter or amend this member. Scope ownership of frame declaration/activation/evaluation/basis/relation/result/coverage/revision/qualification concepts does not redefine imported owner concepts. Nominally matching profiles, Products, roles or runtime carriers are not imported by proximity.

grounding.quote:
A refinement this member states, such as the function outcomes of §5
or the coverage statuses of §8, names its owner in this table and maps
back to it.

constraints.statement: Every listed import runs from its named source member to the reference-frame-evaluation context with no loss, ownership transfer or authority grant. Imported concepts are not defined a second time. Local refinements, including function outcomes and coverage statuses, name and map back to their owner. A profile- or Product-declared frame/family in this context remains that owner's specialisation and is not thereby imported into this member. The declaration is reported new and intended to retain one owning section per concept.

An accepted Project Reference-Frame Basis may be expressed entirely as
source-linked prose.

Optionally bind sprint manifests.

repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints or product-scoped

grounding.quote:
One complete immutable released RC cut of this standards tree is the
constitutional member set of the selectable STDO Product. The release may
also carry subordinate executable and interaction tooling (P6, P3;
provenance rc.2 README #standards-library). A cut carries (P3, P2):

- the constitutional members of tiers 1 and 2 above;
- the carrier-neutral [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md), whose
  a_c theory stays separate from interpreted subject models and carrier
  encodings ([AC-020](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation));
- the application-neutral traversal occurrence profile
  [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md), which instantiates
  one closed model-family signature under an exact a_c basis without
  changing the calculus or selecting a consumer, and whose adoption stays
  optional;
- derived application profiles such as
  [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md);
- the companion guides [POSTING_GUIDE](POSTING_GUIDE.md) and
  [WRITING_GUIDE](WRITING_GUIDE.md);
- the non-deciding semantic locator index [GLOSSARY](GLOSSARY.md), whose
  rows point to the clauses that own each indexed concept and the contexts
  that hold it, and never define a shared default;
- compact read models for activations that need a compact method basis;
  their carrier awaits the ruling on the rc.2 compression rows;
- normative interoperability schemas under `schemas/`, among them the
  layout-neutral product definition overlay and the deterministic

The STDO toolchain manager installs each complete immutable cut once in a
shared versioned store and resolves logical release URIs, so a product
definition names its basis by logical URI and manifest digest and carries
no machine-local path
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager))
(P3, P6). A project-local copy stays possible when it is explicitly bound
and verified; it is not the default
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#12-bootstrap)) (P6, P3).
Installed bytes take their authority from the exact RC cut, the product
definition's basis URI, the manifest digest and the member inventory
([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager),
[RELEASE §3](RELEASE.md#exact-cut-qualification)) (P3, P6). Neither the
mutable authoring head nor the moving version-line selector silently
replaces that consumer basis
([RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption)) (P6, P3).
